anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet the USB-C receptacle J12 VBUS pin (A4) carries the global label 'VBUS' and, on the same wire, the '+5V' power symbol. On the Power sheet U5 (TPS2121RUXR) pin 1 (OUT) is also labelled 'VBUS' while pin 2 (IN2) is labelled '+5V'. Because '+5V' and 'VBUS' are joined at the connector, the mux's USB input (IN2) and its output (OUT) end up on the same net.
anomalies.expected: The specification keeps these two rails separate: 'J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2)' and 'outputs a single OUT ... onto the VBUS net ... (the board's internal, unregulated/pre-buck rail - note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux)'.

evidence.quote: J12 A4 -> VBUS (global label) with +5V power symbol on the same wire (mcu.kicad_sch); U5 pin1 OUT -> VBUS, U5 pin2 IN2 -> +5V (power.kicad_sch)
J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2) ... outputs a single OUT ... onto the VBUS net ... distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux

anomalies.impact: The power mux cannot arbitrate: its IN2 (USB leg) is shorted to its OUT, and the raw USB VBUS is tied directly to the mux output / buck input. The board will not run from USB alone, and when the barrel jack is connected the mux output (12 V) back-feeds into the USB-C VBUS pin, violating the intended seamless-switchover and the input-isolation design.

anomalies.observed: U1 pin 8 (EN/CHIP_PU) is connected to +3V3 through C14, a two-plate capacitor symbol, and to GND through C7 (10 uF). There is no resistive DC path from +3V3 to the EN pin. The resistor the spec assigns to the EN function, R2, is instead wired to the TP4/TP5 / U0TXD-U0RXD node (with R11).
anomalies.expected: The EN/CHIP_PU pin must be pulled up to +3V3 with a resistor so the chip enables at power-on; the spec lists R2 among the 'pull-up/pull-down resistors R2/R5/R6/R11 (strapping/EN/fan-tach related)'. A capacitor in this position provides no DC pull-up.

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch: +3V3 -> C14 (capacitor) -> node = U1 pin 8 EN/CHIP_PU = C7 top; C7 (10uF) -> GND; R2/R11 tied to TP4/TP5 and U1 pins 31/30, not to pin 8
+3V3 net feeds ... pull-up/pull-down resistors R2/R5/R6/R11 (strapping/EN/fan-tach related ...)

anomalies.impact: With EN coupled to +3V3 only through a capacitor and held to GND by C7, the enable pin sits at 0 V at DC, so the ESP32-C3 is held in reset and the board never boots / runs firmware.

parsed.summary: Two deviations from the intended design are visible on the drawing: the USB +5V rail and the mux output VBUS net are merged at J12 (shorting TPS2121 IN2 to OUT and defeating the power-mux arbitration), and the ESP32-C3 EN/CHIP_PU pin is DC-coupled to +3V3 through a capacitor (C14) with no pull-up resistor, leaving the MCU held in reset.
